facts.fact: Founded in 1982 by Mike Graham, a Yosemite 'Stonemaster' climber; it started in a garage in Ventura, California.

The first product was a climbing short: a diamond-shaped gusset taken from kung-fu trousers for full 180-degree flexibility, hard-wearing canvas, and an integrated nylon webbing belt (inspired by backpack straps) adjustable with one hand over an elasticated waist.
The name comes from a moniker Graham gave himself when a few Stonemasters attempted the first 'all-Italian' ascent of Half Dome (none of them were Italian).

After the shorts came the trousers, dubbed the G-Pants; by the mid-80s surfers and skaters were seeking out the pants with the hand-drawn 'running man' logo. The brand later found favor in Tokyo and moved its home to Japan.
Gramicci Products' first items were big-wall accessories such as haul bags and belay seats; Graham's mother taught him to sew, and he cites Bruce Lee as an influence on the early trousers.
The Stonemasters were the first to climb El Capitan in a day and made the first free ascent of Astroman in Yosemite Valley.
TGI's existing Brand to Know on Gramicci (Aug 2026) covers the original Gramicci Pant, G-Short and cotton range; its brand facts match the brand's About page above.

quotes.quote: For me, building clothing is like architecture and engineering. And those were the ideas I put into Gramicci, to make things function in a better way.
Yes, form was never the criteria for the product. It was all based on the function and then I guess we were lucky to get the form right as well!
40 years since the first pair of Gramicci shorts were sewn together in Mike Graham's garage, the song remains the same—it's hard-wearing, functional clothing, designed with movement firmly in mind.

lookbook.desc: Archive-style shot on a snowy mountain scree slope: a magnifying glass held over the Gramicci label on a climber's pants (gramicci.com homepage hero). Best hero candidate.
El Capitan above the trees with a Yosemite tour bus in the foreground (Journal: In Conversation with Mike Graham).
Two people walking away through a tall-grass meadow toward a dark pine treeline, in a striped fleece and a graphic tee (FW26 Journal).
Motion-blurred rider in a navy jacket pedalling through a splashing stream (FW26 Journal) — the wet-weather mood.
Climber bouldering an overhanging mossy rock in a purple top and orange pants (FW26 Journal).
Archival 1970s photo: three climbers in fleece and headbands resting on granite slabs among climbing gear (Gramicci book images, Journal: In Conversation with Mike Graham).

Its Nylon Gramicci Cap (nylon-gramicci-cap-1) and Cliff Pant (stretch 98% cotton/2% PU, $104-138, the only in-stock stretch pant) were deliberately left out; Nylon Gramicci Cap ($59, recycled nylon, water repellent) is a swap if a cap with the webbing belt is wanted.
